verdicts.summary: If any secret-store read fails, the changes stream sends the unmaterialized settings to subscribers. The provider registry then rebuilds the Antigravity instance with the redaction marker as its API key. This now affects `config.apiKey`, which until this change was stored as plain text.
verdicts.scenario: 1) An Antigravity instance has a saved apiKey, so the cached settings hold `••••••`. 2) The user saves any setting, which calls emitChange(next). 3) In materializeChanges, secretStore.get fails for any secret (the key, or a GitHub token: materialize is all-or-nothing). 4) The catch logs a warning and emits the raw `settings`, which still contain the markers. 5) ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration reconciles with that config. AntigravityDriver builds auth with apiKey `••••••`, and antigravityAuthSupport exports GEMINI_API_KEY=`••••••` to the CLI. The validity check passes because the marker is not empty.
verdicts.consequence: Antigravity sessions fail authentication with a bogus key, and the status check does not flag it. This lasts until the next settings change materializes successfully. Usage-limit sources get the same fallback and send the marker as the hub key, but that part is older behaviour.

verdicts.summary: The load-time move keeps the value in plain text when the store write fails, and rewrites the file only for secrets that were actually moved. Client redaction does not depend on the move succeeding.
verdicts.scenario: I tried a failed secretStore.set for the Antigravity key. moved stays empty, the function returns the settings unchanged, and nothing is rewritten for it. redact still hides the value because the value is not empty. A later save that echoes the marker picks up the inline value through `previous` and writes it to the store (persist 956-959). I also tried a partial success: only the names in `moved` are replaced (714-716). Downgrading to an older server would read the marker as the credential, but that is a deliberate format change.

verdicts.summary: The only hazard is the card/dialog branches passing the marker as `value` without `configured`, which finding 0 already reports. The other SecretInput callers I checked pass `configured` correctly and use a value that is empty when redacted: the ProviderInstanceCard environment rows (266/293, 428/431), the GitHub token dialog (41/110), and the AddUsageLimitSource draft. Every ProviderSettingsForm caller uses variant="settings".

`decodeTo` keeps the `to` schema's context. It only adds an encoding link on `to`, and `copy` keeps `context`. So `secretSetting` applied before `withDecodingDefault` survives, and the later `annotateKey` merges into it.
verdicts.scenario: Antigravity `apiKey` and the GitCafe `token` are built as secretSetting → withDecodingDefault → annotateKey. withDecodingDefault calls decodeTo(self) (Schema.ts:5911), then SchemaAST.decodeTo → appendTransformation → replaceEncoding(to, ...). That copies `to` with only a new encoding, so the context holding settingsSecret stays. annotateKey then spreads the existing context annotations (4408). resolveAnnotationsKey reads ast.context.annotations (Schema.ts:15959). The test at serverSettings.test.ts:1488-1491 also checks that config-secret and gitcafe-secret are not on disk.
